A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same research, renamed from TransProQA to LiTransProQA. Their main texts, figures, tables, and appendices support reliable comparison, including matching retained experiments and question lists across renumbering.

before.justification: V1 reports original metric evaluations on three literary translation datasets, XCOMET finetuning experiments, professional translator ratings, and comparisons across prompting templates and base models.

after.justification: V4 retains these empirical results and adds TREQA-QE evaluations, question-aspect ablations, translator-agreement analysis, significance tests, and qualitative examples.

M1.justification: The question-selection procedure, 25 selected questions, prompting templates, answer-to-score mapping, and translator weighting remain unchanged. XCOMET losses and layer configurations also match. Renaming the metric and analyzing question subsets do not establish a revised proposed method.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate on LITEVAL-CORPUS, LITERARYTRAN, and PAR3-ANNOTATED and finetune using PAR3-UNANNOTATED and WMT24. Language coverage and literary translation tasks are retained; the added analyses use existing coverage.

E2.justification: V4 adds TREQA-QE to the LITEVAL-CORPUS and LITERARYTRAN comparisons in Tables 3–4; v1 discussed TREQA but explicitly deferred evaluating it. Existing baselines remain, and the PAR3-ANNOTATED comparator set is unchanged.

E3.justification: The new ablation protocol scores each of six question aspects alone and excludes each aspect in turn on LITERARYTRAN (Section 5.3). Existing dataset splits, evaluation metrics, finetuning budgets, and base-model configurations remain unchanged; relocated development-set details do not indicate a new split.

E4.justification: V4 substantially expands diagnostic evidence through aspect-isolation and aspect-removal ablations, agreement analysis comparing all versus selected questions, and qualitative success and failure cases (Table 5, Figure 3, Tables 15–16). These examine component contributions, expert consistency, and template-specific failures beyond v1's retained analyses.

E5.justification: V4 introduces permutation-test significance reporting against the best baseline in Table 3, significance assessments of translator weighting in Section A.3.8, and pairwise Pearson/Kendall agreement distributions among translators. V1 lacks these statistical assessments. No increase in repeated runs or seeds is documented.

E6.justification: Original benchmark rows remain unchanged, but v4 adds substantial results for TREQA-QE, ablations, agreement, significance, and qualitative cases. For example, removing tone/authorial-voice questions yields ACC-EQ 0.428 versus 0.519 for the full set. V4 also corrects prose summaries: LITEVAL adequacy gains of 15.2/16.9 points become 14.7/16.4, matching the retained table.

T1.justification: No mathematical definitions, training losses, theorems, or proofs are substantively changed. V4's explanations of correlation-metric suitability and agreement reporting add rationale rather than new formal derivations.

C1.justification: The core claims remain a reference-free, translator-informed QA metric, stronger evaluation performance, benefits from translator weighting, and applicability to open models. V4 foregrounds the student-level human benchmark and professional-performance gap already acknowledged in v1 Section 5.2; the scientific contribution is not redefined.

C2.justification: V4 adds interpretations of complementary question aspects, hypotheses explaining limited XCOMET adaptation, and failure explanations involving cultural context and prompt complexity (Sections 5.3, A.2.3, A.4). It also discusses expert disagreement and adds qualifications concerning genre/style variation, broader audiences, and deployment risks.

D1.justification: V4 newly specifies the mt-metrics-eval version and commit, metadata modification, dependency versions, annotator background details, and code licensing. It updates the code/data repository location and explicitly states split availability. Existing finetuning hyperparameters and development-set sizes are retained.

R1.justification: V4 adds AskQE to the QA-metric discussion and references Alexander, Ji et al., and Eger et al. for statistical reporting and broader context. The ChatEval discussion/reference is removed. Positioning around professional question design remains substantially the same; AskQE is not an evaluated baseline.

P1.justification: V4 renames the metric, edits and condenses passages, moves some dataset and development details into Appendix A, and adds descriptive subsections. The main introduction–related work–datasets–methods–results–conclusion structure and much of the narrative remain intact.

P2.justification: Figure 1 expands from a small first-page column figure to a full-width overview. V4 adds an ablation table, agreement plots, and two extensive qualitative tables, while reorganizing appendix displays and adding significance markers. New Figure 4 visualizes the existing weighting comparison rather than introducing a separate experiment.

improvement.justification: V4 substantially strengthens validation of the unchanged method. The directly relevant TREQA-QE comparison, statistical assessments, aspect ablations, and explicit failure cases address important gaps in v1's evidence for comparative performance and professional question design. Corrected numerical summaries and clearer reproducibility information further improve reliability. Dataset coverage and existing generalization limitations remain unchanged.
